subject: journey/polo
prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset: illustrated journey sketchbook card.
Style: An illustrated page from an explorer's journal: one particular moment on the journey, drawn close enough to see faces, hands, tools, clothing and the things being traded, measured or found. The traveller need not appear: some pages record only what the party saw (a harbour, a fortress, a market, an animal or plant). When the traveller does appear, draw them in action and in a natural, varied pose, not standing to attention. In the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries. A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink with loose hatching; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green, faded blue and a touch of red. The page may carry one or two small separate studies of a detail (an object, a tool, a creature) loosely arranged beside the main scene, as on a real sketchbook page. Edges unfinished, dissolving into bare, slightly foxed cream paper; a single page, no binding visible. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, numbers, dates or signature; any writing that appears in the scene is illegible marks. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given; people, dress and objects true to their place and time, drawn with respect. Landscape aspect ratio 3:2. Strongly visible hand-drawn graphite and ink, exposed cream paper, limited thin watercolor, NOT photorealism. Use exactly one coherent scene and perspective, no extra inset unless requested. Pay attention to anatomically connected arms, load-bearing architecture, boat hulls, rigging and horizontal circular objects. No lettering or typography.
Place: Samara (Samudra), Sumatra. Approximate route year: 1291. Scene: Shore-level sheltered view tropical rain curtains over northern Sumatra anchorage, ships silhouettes beyond wet palm leaves, woven baskets raised on timber supports foreground, no shipbuilding lesson or giant waves inside calm bay.
Marco Polo does NOT appear. The named landscape, object, animal or local activity is the subject; do not add a recurring explorer portrait.
Historical constraints: late thirteenth-century materials, ships, clothes and buildings only. No modern tourism infrastructure, modern instruments, later Ming/Qing buildings, or romantic fantasy scenery. The illustration must be spatially coherent.
